CIDR ranges are supported too — e.g. 0.0.0.0/24 scans the whole range.
Forces DNS queries over TCP/53 instead of UDP/53. Use it only when UDP is blocked, as it is slower. When off, TCP is still used where UDP fails.
Maximum packet size for the VPN tunnel. Auto measures your network and picks the best size. Try 1280 if pages stall or load slowly, or 1500 for faster downloads on a stable connection.
Maximum downstream data one DNS answer may carry. Auto lets the app probe up to 1232 bytes. Try a smaller value if apps stall or load slowly on a lossy network.

A DNS-tunnel VPN client based on Soar,\nby Break The Barriers.
Built for total blackouts,\nwhen DNS is the only way out.
If Unbar helped you, a small donation keeps it going.
Keeps the Unbar DNS tunnel active in the background
Tap + to add a new server: enter the server name, zone, and the server\'s public key. Without a server, you cannot connect.
Instead of entering the details by hand, import an unbar:// link or scan a QR code of the config; the server is added automatically.
Enter a subscription link and the server list will update automatically from that link. Servers you added by hand are left untouched.
The latency test measures how fast each server responds. Auto-select picks the fastest server for the connection.
Tap a server to edit or delete it. Export config shares a server\'s config as a link or a QR code.
Local SOCKS proxy and bandwidth limit

VPN mode routes all of the phone\'s traffic through the tunnel; SOCKS mode only serves apps that have the proxy configured. You can also switch it from the status card on Home — switching while connected reconnects in the new mode. For everyday use, choose VPN mode.
Forces DNS queries over TCP/53 instead of UDP/53. Use it only when UDP is blocked, as it is slower. When off, TCP is still used where UDP fails.

MTU is the size of network packets on the tunnel (default Auto). In Auto, the active interface MTU is measured and 200 bytes are subtracted (clamped to 1280–1500); the new value applies on the next connection. Usually there is no need to change it.
The maximum size of each DNS answer (default Auto). Auto picks the best value; change it only if you have a problem.
Resolvers are the DNS servers the tunnel uses. Built-in uses the built-in list of Iranian resolvers; in Custom mode only the resolvers you entered yourself are used.

The Scan resolvers button checks the resolvers in three stages: first DNS and RTT screening, then a Soar handshake on all stage-1 responders (the verified count rises live and it works even before connecting), and finally ranking and saving every verified resolver into one pool. The Active resolvers card shows how many resolvers are currently carrying traffic — dead ones are replaced automatically, so there is no need to scan again.
While the VPN is connected, a SOCKS proxy also runs on the phone (default port 1080). Set it in your browser or other apps so that only that app uses the tunnel.
Limits the maximum upload and download speed of the tunnel, in KB/s. 0 means no limit.
Connects Iranian domains and IPs directly, without sending them through the tunnel, so domestic sites open faster. If the direct connection fails within 5 seconds, it falls back to the tunnel.
Write the domains or IPs you want to keep out of the tunnel here, one per line.
Chooses which apps use the VPN and which do not. For example, you can route only the browser through the tunnel.

Checks whether a newer release is available. If you are on the latest version, you will see a confirmation; if a newer version is available, a dialog shows the version and what\'s new. Tap Download to fetch the APK and install it — you may first need to allow Unbar to install unknown apps.

The log page (Settings > System & diagnostics > View logs) shows only the entries you need by default — connection events, errors, warnings, your own actions, and scan results. The repeating technical lines that arrive every 20 seconds are hidden; turn on "Show details" to see them. Copying the log still copies everything.
The status card shows whether the tunnel is up and which server you are on. Tap the footer to connect or disconnect. If no server is configured, add your own server first — the app ships with none.
While connected, the card shows the server\'s IP address and country. The country is looked up from the server\'s IP, so it tells you where your traffic exits.

VPN mode routes all of the phone\'s traffic through the tunnel; Proxy mode only serves apps that have the proxy configured. Switching modes while connected takes about 10 seconds: the tunnel disconnects, waits 6 seconds for the old service to stop fully, then reconnects in the new mode. While disconnected, switching only stores the mode for the next connect. For everyday use, choose VPN mode.
Live speeds on the wire, as actually sent through the tunnel.
Latency is the round-trip time to your server, measured through the tunnel. Lower is better; under 200 ms feels fast.
A score from 0 to 100 built from path health, latency and loss. The shield shows the same score in five bars: more lit bars, a better connection.
How many resolvers are currently carrying traffic. Dead ones are replaced automatically, so there is no need to scan again.
Checks the resolvers in three stages: DNS and RTT screening, a Soar handshake on all responders, and saving every verified resolver into one pool.
How much data the tunnel has carried today. The counter resets at midnight.
How much data this session has carried, up and down combined. It keeps counting across reconnects.
How long the current session has been up. It restarts on every reconnect.
How many streams the tunnel is currently carrying. More streams usually means more apps or downloads active.
